newsitem.title: USA: Former Texaco employee sues company for libel.
newsitem.headline: Former Texaco employee sues company for libel.

text.p: A former Texaco Inc executive on Tuesday filed a libel suit against the company in connection with last year's widely publicized race discrimination case.

The suit, filed by former Texaco senior assistant treasurer David Keough, asks for $52 million plus punitive damages. The cause of the action was libel, intentional infliction of emotional distress, wrongful termination and other charges, Keough's lawyer said.

"We filed a suit today against Texaco, (Texaco's chief executive officer) Peter Bijur, and Linda Robinson and her company, Robinson Lerer Montgomery, a public relations firm hired by Texaco after last year's case," said Blair Fensterstock, Keough's attorney.

"We have attempted to negotiate with Texaco and Texaco has refused to negotiate. They have shown a total lack of respect for Mr. Keough and used him for a scapegoat to deal with their PR nightmare," said Fensterstock.
In a statement in response to the suit the company said: "Texaco believes this suit is completely without merit and Texaco will defend itself vigorously."
Keough was fired in January, 1997 from his position as chief financial and administrative officer of Heddington Insurance Co, a Bermuda-based subsidiary of Texaco.

The the basis of his dismissal was a finding by Michael Armstong, the lawyer commissioned by Texaco to look into the discrimination allegations, that Keough participated in the withholding of documents related to the case when he was a senior assistant treasurer at Texaco in 1994.
Fensterstock says Keough denies the allegations and contends in his suit that Texaco's lawyers were "negligent" in failing to produce documents which Keough made available.
The case is expected to take several months to come to trial if it can't be settled, Fensterstock said.
